translit:
Jug sharapo jogade | gurjar khand gumar ||
shap utaro Jivana | leeno Padmanabh avatar ||128||
Gurjar khandman pragate | gyani Gorakhnath ||
das Kabire Jivana | mastak deeno hath ||129||
Gyanike prabodhamen | uda Jivandas ||
aan marag sab chhandke | Sitapatiki aash ||130||
Dev risheshwar poojke | sabki padi vat ||
sab jug bhulyo Jivana | Rame kiyo utpat ||131||
Sab sadhanman Jivana | Ram nam tattvasar ||
Ajamil ganika tari | te ved na lahe lagar ||132||
Tanman sate Hari mile | to jano aasan ||
ant jayego Jivana | narak dehi nirvan ||133||
Kuvalayo maro Jivana | Kanse deeno roy ||
tat bicharo kaha kare | janani Kalayavan mukh joy ||134||
Kuvalayo mal marke | tode Kansake shish ||
Lank Vibhishan thapiyo | so jan Jivanke Ish ||135||
Mukh marun ta dasko | ninda kare jo koy ||
Vaikunthathi darahu | Jivan yun barad mohe ||136||
Ankh faruke Jivana | sab duniya fana mukam ||
sab juthi baji dekhiye | sache Ram Rahman ||137||
Ram Rahman je jape | jake hoy guru pir ||
guru pir nahi Jivana | je bhut pret sharir ||138||
Sadguru samjhayo Jivana | Sitapatiko nam ||
Ajamil ganika tari | le re andhe nam ||139||
Baiyan biji var | nahi hoy aiso davado ||
maya malse kanee var | pan nahi hoy sant melavado ||140||
Indri aparadhan Jivana | bohotek kare burai ||
manav ketoek bapado | jo surnar mele khai ||141||
Ram nam bhaj Jivana | je Anjanisutke Ish ||
hatya utari Lankeshki | je Shiv nirmalya shish ||142||
Deh barabar kot ber | hem tol jo det ||
so Shiv nirmalya Jivana | jo Harijansun nahi het ||143||
Kanak Mer arpan kare | sonpe garath bhandar ||
kahat Kabir guru bahirmukh | so kyun kar pave par ||144||
Guru gumare kaha sarya | takyo swarath aap ||
atam dharam bin Jivana | bohor lagayo pap ||145||
Sitapati Raghunathko | bharunso karo mat koy ||
jutho jano Jivano | to kushal kahanse hoy ||146||
Ghar bhitare agh chhipayke | maya det duray ||
ant bhandi vado Jivana | pahele kyun na karay ||147||
Jivan jug bahe jane de | kar Raghupatisu preet ||
Sadguru hamare yun kahyo | kalikal viparit ||148||
Ek Allathi do bhaya | ko ghoda ko mir ||
e aato saato Jivana | nar samajhat nahi bepir ||149||
Ek palakman sab kiya | trilok brahmand ekvish ||
Harijan kartan Jivana | lage din das vish ||150||
Khaya piya bahut karen | indri swarath dharm ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | kate na eku karm ||151||
Gadi chhanhe lundiyu | jane khinchatahu moye ||
Hari samaran dhori Jivana | to bharam pado mat koy ||152||
Ja mukhathi amrit chuge | so bura bola kyam jay ||
bura bolat hai Jivana | jahan guru pir nahi sahay ||153||
Ved katebathi Jivana | nyare Harike das ||
swarg narak Vaikunth tyaj | kare Hari charanki aash ||154||
Dudh bhat sab det hai | pan aapa koi nav det ||
aapa ubha Jivana | tyon lu bhojan pret ||155||
Jain panth sab Jivana | jahan karm dharmki aash ||
juthi baji khelatan | sab jug jay niraash ||156||
Jain panth sab Jivana | jahan nahi Harike das ||
ko karm dharm kachhu karo | pan swarg narakman vas ||157||
Rajas tamas sattvik | trigun bhakti sansar ||
trigun rahit je Jivana | te Sadguruko upkar ||158||
Tan man arpe Jivana | jake take hath ||
kalpavrikshakun tyajke | devat baval bath ||159||
Abhe vrat ekadashi | nit nit Ganga nahay ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | kal kaleja mahen ||160||
Ekadashi lundi karun | tirath karun gulam ||
nayane Ramaiya rami rahya | tinsun karun salam ||161||
Ekadashi janun nahi | bharam pada sab koy ||
man le bandhe dwadashi | mukti kahan the hoy ||162||
Vasan phute Jivana | vastu na ave hath ||
duniya sab dhandhe padi | van Harijan kyon Rughnath ||163||
Pichhe nipayo atma | kare bhanda vishram ||
mukh dant diya Jivana | tun kahe na jape Raghuram ||164||
Karunanidhi Hari namki | lok karat hai laj ||
chhutat hai budh bahare | jyon jalman chhutat jahaj ||165||
Diya lije Jivana | je deve lakh kod ||
an diya haram hai | na lije tinka tod ||166||
Lakshmi charan seva kare | chaud lok shirtaj ||
Bal dware Hari Jivana | te teen panvke kaj ||167||
Je jaisi kare Jivana | taku taisi hoy ||
Bal chhalayatan aape chhalya | kapat karo mat koy ||168||
Bharam bhramula chhand de | le ohankarki aad ||
Sadguru baith lakhaiya | Jivan jahan badbhag ||169||
Dhik janani tat dhik | dhik sakal parivar ||
gam tham dhik Jivana | je kahe Raghupati avatar ||170||
Baio budhapo dhunkado | samaro Sitaram ||
heli hamchi khundatan | janam gayo bekam ||171||
Vate vadan hot hai | adad sahuke gher ||
ta paheli Jivana | ladakan mandi red ||172||
Chaturbhujkun ko bhaje | ko ashtabhujkun dhyay ||
Ram nam bhaj Jivana | je Gokul charave gay ||173||
Kon karmathe Jivana | kalyo na Jadupati ray ||
Prahlad pidyo tat jab | tab Raghupati bhae na sahay ||174||
Jihva kari kari pap kahe | antargatman bap ||
aiso jagatmen Jivana | beta beti maha pap ||175||
Jodo jado na taryo | pakha pakhika khel ||
tal pile bin Jivana | kaiso nikse tel ||176||
Donu gai re Jivana | gadhe aur brahmachar ||
Ram bhakti jani nahi | chhodyo kul achar ||177||
Chhar chhabi sab Jivana | jahan Harijanka nahi vas ||
kahan ghoda kahan chhapari | kahan mota Kailas ||178||
Sant sangat bhave nahi | kare muktiki aas ||
pita kahasu kahego Jivana | jo beta jayo das ||179||
Ashtavakra adi dei | Brahma Shukdev Vyas ||
Kans cheri agel Jivana | sab ko ho gaye das ||180||
Yun bane nahi Jivana | kuladiman phode gol ||
aapa sate Hari bhaje | manu je Hariko kol ||181||
Dekh tamasa Jivana | lambe panu pasar ||
Harijan sahuko hadmade | te van kripa Kartar ||182||
Ghoda hathi dekhke | manahi bhulano mir ||
charm pos sab Jivana | nar samajhat nahi bepir ||183||
Ek gehuke Jivana | bohotek hoy pakvan ||
Sitapati to ek hai | pan jude jude nam ||184||
Duniya bole Jivana | je raho duniyake pas ||
hamare raja Ram hai | je Lakshmi charan nivas ||185||
Aapa ularan bhajiye | yun karo gharvas ||
manav janam tano fal le re | kar sant sangat nivas ||186||
Bhala kare so aapkun | bura kare saheya ||
donuthi nyara Jivana | jahan Sitapatiko jap ||187||
Mukh shiyala sunghke | mada diya bahay ||
mukhse Ram na ocharo | to Jivan kyon patiyay ||188||
Lankeshwar maryo Jivana | so sur munijanke kaj ||
Lank Vibhishan thapiyo | ek panth do kaj ||189||
Bhagat manorath Jivana | kaha kaha kiyo Raghuvir ||
kabahuk jyot swarup bhaye | kabahuk dharyo sharir ||190||
Sita karan Jivana | maryo Ravan rank ||
khila bale bankiye | dei Vibhishan Lank ||191||
translation:
128. The yogi laid a curse upon the age; the land of Gujarat was steeped in pride. To lift that curse, O Jivana, the Lord took birth as Padmanabh.

129. In the land of Gujarat appeared the wise Gorakhnath; and Das Kabir, O Jivana, laid his hand upon his head.

130. At the awakening given by the wise one, Jivandas arose; leaving all other paths behind, he set his hope on Sitapati (the Lord of Sita, Ram).

131. Worshipping gods and great sages, everyone has beaten those well-worn tracks; the whole age has gone astray, O Jivana - Ram has thrown it all into an uproar.

132. Among all spiritual disciplines, O Jivana, the name of Ram is the very essence of truth; Ajamil and the courtesan crossed over by it - something the Vedas do not grasp in the least.

133. If Hari is obtained at the price of body and mind, know it to be cheaply had; in the end all will depart, O Jivana - the body of flesh ends either in hell or in nirvana (final release).

134. He slew the elephant Kuvalaya, O Jivana, and left Kans weeping. What could the poor father do? - the mother looked into the face of Kalayavan.

135. Having slain the elephant Kuvalaya and the wrestlers, he broke off Kans's head; he set Vibhishan upon Lanka - He is the Lord of His servant Jivana.

136. "I strike the mouth of the one who slanders My servant; I cast him out of Vaikunth" - such, O Jivana, is the vow (birad) He holds to for my sake.

137. In the blink of an eye, O Jivana, the whole world is a place of perishing; all that we see is a false game - true are Ram and Rahman.

138. He who repeats Ram and Rahman - he has a guru, a pir (Muslim spiritual master). Without guru or pir, O Jivana, the body is nothing but ghost and spirit.

139. The Sadguru (true master) made me understand, O Jivana, the name of Sitapati; Ajamil and the courtesan crossed over - take up that Name, O blind one.

140. Sisters, such an opportunity will not come a second time; wealth (maya) you will meet many times over, but the gathering of saints will not come again.

141. The senses are the offenders, O Jivana; they work a great deal of evil. What is a poor man's strength worth, when they fling gods and men alike into the pit?

142. Chant the name of Ram, O Jivana - He who is the Lord of Anjani's son (Hanuman); He wiped away the sin of slaying Lanka's lord - the lord whose heads were laid before Shiv as nirmalya (offerings made over to the deity).

143. Though a man give gold weighed out ten million times against his own body, it is only Shiv's cast-off offering, O Jivana, if he has no love for Hari's devotees.

144. Though he offer a Meru of gold and hand over his whole treasury - says Kabir - if he has turned his face away from the guru, how shall he reach the far shore?

145. What is gained by pride before the guru? He has cast aside his own true interest. Without the dharma of the soul, O Jivana, he has heaped up sin all over again.

146. Put your trust in Sitapati Raghunath and in no one else; if you hold Him false, O Jivana, from where can well-being come?

147. Hiding his sin within the house, he keeps his wealth concealed; in the end it is all laid bare, O Jivana - why not have done rightly at the first?

148. Jivana, let the world flow on by; make your love with Raghupati. So our Sadguru told us: the age of Kali runs contrary to all good.

149. From the one Allah the two came into being - one a horse, one a lord (mir); this is the bargain and the barter, O Jivana - and man, having no pir, does not understand it.

150. In a single instant He made everything - the three worlds and the twenty-one universes; but in the making of a devotee of Hari, O Jivana, ten or twenty days are spent.

151. People eat and drink their fill and make the self-interest of the senses their religion; without Sitapati, O Jivana, not a single karma is cut away.

152. The little dog walking in the cart's shadow thinks that he is the one pulling it; the remembrance of Hari is the ox that draws the load, O Jivana - so let no one fall into that delusion.

153. The mouth from which nectar drips - how should foul speech come out of it? Foul words are spoken, O Jivana, where guru and pir give no help.

154. Apart from Veda and Kateb (the Semitic scriptures), O Jivana, stand the servants of Hari; renouncing heaven, hell and Vaikunth alike, they long only for Hari's feet.

155. Everyone gives milk and rice, but no one gives up his own self (apa, egoity); while the ego stands there, O Jivana, the food is a ghost's fare.

156. All of it is the Jain path, O Jivana, wherever the hope rests in rite and merit; playing at that false game, the whole age goes away disappointed.

157. All of it is the Jain path, O Jivana, where there are no servants of Hari; work what rites and merit you please, the dwelling is still heaven or hell.

158. Rajasic, tamasic, sattvic - the world's bhakti (devotion) is bound to the three gunas (qualities of nature); to be free of the three gunas, O Jivana, is the Sadguru's gift of grace.

159. He hands over body and mind, O Jivana, into this hand and that; leaving the wish-granting tree, he embraces the thorny babul.

160. Though one keep vows and the ekadashi fast and bathe in the Ganga day after day, without Sitapati, O Jivana, death sits inside the heart.

161. I make ekadashi my maidservant and pilgrimage my slave; the Beloved (Ramaiya) plays before my eyes - it is to Him I make my salaam.

162. I know no ekadashi; everyone has fallen into delusion. If a man binds his mind to the twelfth-day rite, from where is liberation to come?

163. The vessel is broken, O Jivana, and the substance never comes to hand. The whole world has fallen into its business - without becoming Hari's devotee, how is one to reach Raghunath?

164. The soul was fashioned afterwards; it takes its rest inside the vessel of the body. He gave you a mouth and teeth, O Jivana - why then do you not repeat Raghuram?

165. People feel ashamed at the name of Hari, the treasury of compassion; the witless drift away, as a ship slips loose upon the water.

166. Take what is given, O Jivana, though it be lakhs and crores that he gives; what is not given is haram (forbidden) - do not take so much as a broken straw of it.

167. Lakshmi serves at His feet; He is the crown of the fourteen worlds - yet Hari stood at Bali's door, O Jivana, for the sake of three paces of ground.

168. As a man does, O Jivana, so it is done back to him; in tricking Bali He was Himself caught by the trick - so let no one practise deceit.

169. Give up delusion and its wanderings; take up the primal "I am He" (ohankar, soham). The Sadguru sat down and showed it plainly, O Jivana - there lies great good fortune.

170. Shame on the mother, shame on the father, shame on the whole family; shame on the village and the place, O Jivana, that calls Raghupati merely an avatar (an incarnation).

171. Sisters, old age is drawing close - remember Sitaram; while you romped at hamchi (a girls' folk game) with your friend, the birth has gone to waste.

172. By talk alone the fritters are already made, while the lentils are still in the merchant's shop; and even before that, O Jivana, the children have set up their clamour.

173. Some worship the four-armed one, some meditate on the eight-armed; chant the name of Ram, O Jivana - He who grazes the cows in Gokul.

174. By what karma was it, O Jivana, that Jadupati the king was nowhere to be found? When the father tormented Prahlad, Raghupati did not come to his aid.

175. With his tongue he calls it sin over and over, while inwardly he is its very father; such is the way of the world, O Jivana - son and daughter are a great sin.

176. Neither the one nor the other of the pair got across; it is a game of faction against faction. Without pressing the sesame, O Jivana, how is the oil to come out?

177. Both were lost, O Jivana - the donkey's way and the celibate's; he never came to know devotion to Ram, and he abandoned the conduct of his lineage.

178. All splendour is ashes, O Jivana, where Hari's devotees do not dwell - be it horses, be it a hut, be it great Kailas itself.

179. Satsang (holy company) does not please him, yet he hopes for liberation. To whom shall the father tell it, O Jivana, when the son born to him has turned out a slave?

180. Ashtavakra and the rest, Brahma, Shukdev and Vyas - and on down to Kans's maidservant, O Jivana, every one of them became His servant.

181. It cannot be managed this way, O Jivana - breaking the lump of jaggery inside a little pot (doing it all in secret). Worship Hari at the price of your own self: that I take to be Hari's own covenant (kol).

182. Watch the spectacle, O Jivana, with your legs stretched out at ease; everyone jostles and harries the devotee of Hari - and such people are without the Creator's grace.

183. Looking at his horses and elephants, the lord (mir) grew heedless in his mind; it is all a covering of skin, O Jivana - and man, having no pir, does not understand.

184. Out of one wheat, O Jivana, a great many dishes are made; Sitapati is only One, though the names given Him are many.

185. The world says, O Jivana, "Stay close to the world." Our king is Ram, at whose feet Lakshmi has her dwelling.

186. Flee from the swelling of the ego; keep your household life in that way. Take the fruit of this human birth - make your dwelling in the company of saints.

187. Whoever does good does it for himself; whoever does evil must bear it himself. Apart from both, O Jivana, is the place where Sitapati's name is repeated.

188. The jackals sniffed at the mouth and let the corpse float away; if the mouth does not utter Ram, then, O Jivana, how is it to be trusted?

189. He slew the lord of Lanka, O Jivana, for the sake of gods and sages; and he set Vibhishan upon Lanka - one road, two errands done.

190. What has Raghuvir not done, O Jivana, to fulfil His devotees' longing! Sometimes He became pure light; sometimes He took on a body.

191. For Sita's sake, O Jivana, He slew the wretched Ravan; the nail was bent by force, and He gave Lanka over to Vibhishan.
